cases.frame: Apparent true equator/equinox of date for RA; apparent ecliptic of date for longitude. Interpreted from NAOJ almanac conventions; the CGI does not expose its complete reduction.
qualifications: The Calendar and Ephemeris Office says the web edition uses its latest theory. Its 2026 revision adopts JPL DE440; earlier 2016-2025 editions use DE430. The 2009 revision adopts IAU 2006 precession/nutation. Thus newly queried 2026 web tables use the latest DE-series implementation, not the printed almanac of the event year. No Swiss-derived source is invoked.
Printed resolution is not source accuracy. Use TT directly; do not relabel it UTC.

The first contact-time correction is included in the Boston worked example. A paragraph says omitting this correction can introduce up to one and a half minutes; that does not prove the Washington tables omit it.
geometry.engineMoonRadiusLocator: src/sky/riseset.ts: SKY_RADII_KM.Moon (constant read only, no engine evaluation)
geometry.radiusDifferenceInterpretation: This signed geometric radius difference is independent of contact time. No seconds-of-time bound can be assigned without normal limb-crossing speed.

clock.sourceDefinitionLocator: p. 746: astronomical day begins at noon; astronomical time is used throughout the volume
clock.conversion: Civil date-time = printed astronomical date at midnight + 12 h + printed mean time + west longitude in time (zero for printed Greenwich times).
clock.canonicalScale: UT1 approximation to historical Greenwich mean solar time; not UTC
clock.zSuffixMeaning: The Z suffix is only the parser-compatible timestamp representation. The separately recorded ut1 scale controls semantics.
clock.earthRotationCaveat: The publication predates modern UT1. No UT0/UT1 polar-motion correction or modern time realization is documented; do not imply subsecond equivalence.
clock.washingtonLongitudeChoice: Station 246 west longitude is an explicit inference, shared with observer selection.
